Most people pick a marketing course the wrong way.

A friend's tip. A nice brochure. A start date that fits. Then week three arrives and the pace feels wrong, the examples feel far from real work, and motivation quietly fades.

The course was not always the problem. It just was not built for the way they learn.

In my new article I share what I would check before signing up for any digital marketing course in Mauritius: real work in live ad accounts, current AI content, a trainer who still runs campaigns, MQA approval (which HRDC requires for employer refunds), a recognised certificate and genuine personal feedback.

But the step most people skip matters most. Assess how you learn first.

I built a free assessment for exactly this. It takes about 15 to 20 minutes, needs no marketing knowledge, and finds whether you are a visual, structured, social or hands on learner, plus your starting level. You then get a personalised learning plan covering your pace, feedback style and personal goal.

Twenty minutes now can save you twenty weeks of frustration.
